sources.entry: Dive into Deep Learning - Interactive book with Jupyter and PyTorch. #free

summary.name: Dive into Deep Learning
summary.one_liner: An interactive, open-source deep learning textbook where each section is an executable Jupyter notebook combining math, figures, code and community discussion.
keywords: cambridge university press deep learning book
use_cases: learning deep learning with runnable code
using a textbook in a university course
reference for deep learning math and implementations
following the Berkeley deep learning course materials
comparing framework implementations in PyTorch, JAX or TensorFlow
summary.what_it_does: The page describes an interactive deep learning book in which every section is an executable Jupyter notebook that readers can modify and rerun. Concepts are presented with mathematics, figures, code and text, with experiments on real data sets. The book is implemented in PyTorch, NumPy/MXNet, JAX and TensorFlow. Each section links to a community discussion forum. The page also lists the Berkeley course slides, notebooks and videos, and notes it is used at 500 universities in 70 countries.
notable: Each section is an executable Jupyter notebook for hands-on experimentation
Multiple framework implementations: PyTorch, NumPy/MXNet, JAX, TensorFlow
Free option to run the book via SageMaker Studio Lab
Companion Berkeley course slides, notebooks, assignments and videos
caveats: A print edition is forthcoming from Cambridge University Press, so the print version is not yet available per the page
Chinese and other translations are listed as ongoing, so coverage in some languages may be incomplete
